standard.title: First Nations drama and Country/Place
standard.description: explore how First Nations Australians use drama to communicate their connection to, and responsibility for, Country/Place
standard.prior_knowledge: Students have explored examples of drama created and/or performed by First Nations Australians and attended to how elements communicate cultural meaning (Y1-2). They understand that First Nations Australians use drama to share cultural knowledge.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explore how First Nations Australians use drama to communicate their connection to, and responsibility for, Country/Place.

nodes.label: Drama as expression of Country/Place — what and why
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe what it means for First Nations Australians to communicate connection to and responsibility for Country/Place through drama, and identify examples.
nodes.minimum_width: Student describes one way First Nations drama communicates knowledge about or connection to Country/Place.
nodes.typical_width: Students collect and share information about drama created and performed by First Nations Australians for festivals, ceremonies or cultural occasions; they explore how First Nations Australians use drama to communicate knowledge about the local environment and to maintain unique ways of life.
wider: Students access drama created and/or performed by First Nations Australians and explore how it communicates ways to live sustainably and care for land, sea, sky or waterways
Students explore performances that represent the importance of Country/Place and Story as a starting point for discussing different ways of seeing the same place and telling stories
nodes.hinge_reason: The concept of Country/Place as a living relationship — not just a place on a map — is foundational for understanding First Nations drama; without grasping this, students cannot read the elements of drama in the second node with cultural appropriateness.

response_modes.reason: Use guided discussion and culturally authoritative resources to establish the concept of Country/Place before observing drama; ensure students understand this is about living relationship, not geography.

success_criteria: Student describes at least one way First Nations drama communicates connection to or responsibility for Country/Place
Student identifies a specific drama example (festival, ceremony, storytelling) in which this is expressed

nodes.label: How elements of drama communicate Country/Place
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can observe and describe how elements of drama are used in First Nations drama to communicate connection to and responsibility for Country/Place.
nodes.minimum_width: Student describes how at least one element of drama (movement, language, place) functions in a specific First Nations drama example to communicate cultural meaning.
nodes.typical_width: Students observe how elements of drama — place, language, movement — are used in First Nations drama that shares cultural narratives; they explore how drama communicates knowledge and consider how different ways of seeing the same place produce different stories.
wider: Students compare how the same Country/Place is represented through drama across different First Nations communities, exploring how cultural perspectives shape dramatic choices
Students investigate how First Nations drama performers use specific movement or language conventions tied to cultural knowledge of their country

response_modes.reason: Engage with drama from multiple First Nations communities and cultural contexts — diversity within First Nations Australia is significant and should not be flattened to a single representative example.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: First Nations Australian dramatic traditions are diverse across Country; engaging with multiple examples from different communities builds genuine appreciation of cultural diversity, not a monolithic view.
success_criteria: Student describes how at least one element of drama is used in a First Nations drama to communicate cultural meaning
Student demonstrates respect for cultural context in their description — attends to meaning, not just surface features
